organization.name: ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak

abbreviations.DARE: Department of Agricultural Research and Education

organization.location: Dirang, West Kameng District, Arunachal Pradesh, India
organization.description: ICAR–NRCY is a specialised research institute under ICAR, Government of India, focused on yak research, technology development, conservation, breeding, health, nutrition, production, product value addition and extension.

icar.description: India's apex national organisation for coordinating and promoting agricultural research, education and extension.
icar.under: Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

official_mandate: Identification, conservation, characterisation and evaluation of yak germplasm
Improvement of yak for draught and milk production
Establishment and maintenance of nucleus yak herds
Development of strategies for conservation of yak genetic resources
Research on in-situ and ex-situ conservation of yak genetic resources
Research on yak production, productivity, health and product quality
Research on yak crossbreds traditionally maintained in mid-altitude areas
Development of scientific strategies for yak–cattle crossbreeding
Development and dissemination of technologies for sustainable yak husbandry

farm_and_facilities.important_distinction: NRCY headquarters is at Dirang; the experimental yak farm is at Nyukmadung.

ftai_2026.description: Demonstration of estrus synchronisation and Fixed-Time Artificial Insemination (FTAI) in yaks under field conditions in Sikkim.

ai_iot_2026.description: IoT-based smart system developed with Assam Don Bosco University for yak health monitoring, stress prediction, geo-fencing, real-time monitoring and precision livestock management.

faq.question: What is NRCY?
faq.answer: NRCY stands for ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak. It is a specialised ICAR research institute focused on yak research, conservation, breeding, health, nutrition, production and value addition.

faq.question: Where is NRCY located?
faq.answer: NRCY is located in Dirang, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh, India.

faq.question: Who is the Director of NRCY?
faq.answer: Dr. Mihir Sarkar is the current Director of ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak.

faq.question: Is NRCY part of ICAR?
faq.answer: Yes. ICAR–NRCY is a specialised research institute under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research.

faq.question: Is NRCY a university?
faq.answer: No. NRCY is a research institute under ICAR.

faq.question: Where is the NRCY yak farm?
faq.answer: NRCY has an experimental yak farm at Nyukmadung, approximately 31 kilometres from Dirang, at around 2,750 metres above mean sea level.

faq.question: What does NRCY research?
faq.answer: NRCY researches yak genetics, breeding, nutrition, health, reproduction, production, conservation, fibre, milk and other yak products.

faq.question: What is NRCY's recent AI project?
faq.answer: NRCY and Assam Don Bosco University developed an IoT-based smart system for yak health monitoring, stress prediction and geo-fencing.

faq.question: What is the recent breeding achievement of NRCY?
faq.answer: In 2026, NRCY demonstrated estrus synchronisation and Fixed-Time Artificial Insemination in yaks under field conditions in Sikkim.

faq.question: Does NRCY work outside Arunachal Pradesh?
faq.answer: Yes. NRCY conducts research, extension and technology-transfer activities in other Himalayan yak-rearing regions, including Sikkim and Ladakh.

faq.question: What is yak churpi?
faq.answer: Yak churpi is a traditional product made from yak milk. Arunachal Pradesh Yak Churpi has GI recognition, and NRCY has contributed to its promotion and value addition.
